## Summary: Shared Style Across mdostal's 4 Sites

**1. plugin-hive** (firefly-events.github.io/plugin-hive/) — Single-page, dark-themed marketing landing page with amber/honeycomb accent motifs reinforcing a "swarm" metaphor. Sections: hero w/ logo lockup, "The Roster" (feature cards), "The Pipeline" (workflow steps), architecture deep-dives, "Why Hive" comparison, OSS CTA, footer nav. Tone: technical-but-punchy marketing copy ("Your AI team. Actually a team"). Heaviest visual production of the four (illustrated assets, hex motifs).

**2. codigatchi-site** — Single-page, minimalist/monospace, dark-neutral, terminal-native aesthetic. Hero with tagline + stat badges (20 min MVP, 112 tests, $0 cloud spend), then seven numbered narrative sections on build methodology, ending in a philosophy-statement footer. Tone: technical, dry-witty, peer-to-peer ("Trust the gate, not the report—expect the gate itself to be gamed"). No traditional nav; badges do a lot of credibility work.

**3. tools.mdostal.com** — This IS a hub page. Minimal, light, card-based layout listing four projects (Allergy Locator, Mapstack, Medical Study Tracker, Drone Components), each with a name, one-line description, screenshot, and dual links (live tool + GitHub source). Header has breadcrumb-style nav to `life.mdostal.com` and `mdostal.com`; footer attributes to Mathew Dostal + GitHub. Built on Next.js (image optimization URLs) + Sanity CMS. Tone: terse, benefit-first, no fluff. **Important: it does NOT currently link to plugin-hive or codigatchi-site** — those live under the separate `firefly-events` GitHub org (likely a distinct sub-brand), while tools.mdostal.com only surfaces the `mdostal/*` repos. Medical Study Tracker is the one overlap, linked both to its live app and its GitHub Pages site.

**4. medical-study-tracker** — Single-page, clean monochrome (black-on-white), Tailwind-flavored, minimal nav (live app / GitHub / disclaimer). Hero → dual CTA buttons → screenshot → "the headline number lies" analytical breakdown → six-feature grid → tech stack list → legal disclaimer → footer repeating CTAs. Tone: technical, pragmatic, slyly skeptical of industry norms. Built with Next.js 15 App Router, TypeScript, Tailwind, shadcn/ui, Vitest; no backend, localStorage only.

**Shared elements across all four:** no common CSS framework artifact beyond a general "Tailwind/shadcn-ish" sans-serif minimalism; no shared header/footer chrome (plugin-hive and codigatchi-site are dark/thematic, tools.mdostal.com and medical-study-tracker are light/neutral); consistent voice — direct, technically credible, occasionally dry-humored, zero hype-marketing filler; consistent pattern of dual CTA links (live/demo + GitHub source); MIT/Apache OSS framing; screenshots/stat-badges used as trust signals rather than testimonials.

## Recommendation for gigradar

Model gigradar's GitHub Pages site on the **medical-study-tracker / tools.mdostal.com register** (light, clean, Tailwind-minimalist, single scrolling page) rather than plugin-hive's dark/illustrated theme — gigradar is a practical personal-data tool like Medical Study Tracker, not a dev-tooling swarm product. Structure: hero (one-line value prop + dual CTA "Try it" / "View source"), a "why this matters" skeptical-industry-take section (matching MST's "headline number lies" pattern), a feature grid, a tech-stack line, a disclaimer/privacy note (gigradar handles job-search data — worth it), and a terse footer. Keep copy technical-pragmatic with a touch of dry humor, no marketing hyperbole. Once live, add gigradar as a fifth card on tools.mdostal.com to make the hub pattern complete.
